conceptDrafts.logline: A hospice nurse who prides herself on 'good deaths' starts skimming end-of-life medications for a grieving black market — and her newest patient is the retired pharmacist who trained her.

settings.toneNote: intimate, not operatic — the crime fits in a tote bag

concept.summary: Noor Haddad is the hospice nurse families ask for by name. She is also, eleven months into her mother's unpayable memory-care bills, the person quietly diverting leftover fentanyl patches and lorazepam from the dying to a buyer who supplies other people's good deaths off the books. Her system is exact: never short a patient, never touch the chart, never take from anyone lucid enough to notice. Then she's assigned Walter Reyes — the retired hospital pharmacist who taught her to count, who is dying slowly, lucidly, and who counts everything.

characters.name: Noor Haddad
characters.backstory: Fifteen years of other families' worst nights; her own mother no longer knows her on Tuesdays.
characters.motivations: Keep her mother in the good facility without selling the house her father built.
characters.flaws: Believes her precision makes it mercy instead of theft.
characters.want: Eight more months of payments without getting caught.
characters.need: To let someone witness her instead of managing them.

relationships.description: her mentor — precepted her hospital rotation twenty years ago; now her assigned hospice patient

characters.voice: gentle imperatives; dosage-exact language even about feelings
characters.arc: From immaculate systems to a confession she administers herself.

characters.name: Walter Reyes
characters.backstory: Thirty-eight years behind the hospital pharmacy counter; taught two generations of nurses that counting is a moral act.
characters.motivations: Die with his ledger balanced — and every count in his orbit accurate.
characters.flaws: Would rather be correct than comforted, even now.
characters.want: To know why his patch schedule is eleven minutes off.
characters.need: To spend his last accuracy on grace instead of a verdict.

relationships.description: his best student; he recognizes her diversion pattern because he invented the audit that catches it

characters.voice: pharmacist's murmur; questions phrased as inventory
